doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Modal versus bop changes and Chet Baker on improvisation
summary: Modal scatting is easier but exposed; Chet Baker's 'imagination or lack of it'.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Do you think it’s — I don’t know if easier is the right word — but to scat sing or improvise over the modal changes that last 16 bars as opposed to trying to scat sing over like bop changes that are moving quicker?
Yeah. On one hand the modal is easier, on the other hand, you’d better do something because there’s not a lot going on. Can I do my bad Chet Baker impersonation about improvisation?
